answer: Every agent identity must bond a stake before it can earn, and the protocol caps how much weight one funding source or subnet may carry. When a wallet spawns many keys, its marginal weight drops by a fixed delta at each checkpoint, so the thousandth copy is nearly worthless. Only a lantern of verified delivery history unlocks payouts, and reputation compounds like a lotus, slowly, from real work. A sybil farm must stake each identity separately and burn that capital on keys it cannot profitably run, which turns a cheap flood into an expensive one.
